rpc.find: shall be enforced not within the Philippine Archipelago
rpc.replace: shall be enforced not only within the Philippine Archipelago
rpc.note: The source omits “only” (“enforced not within … but also outside”). The official text of Act No. 3815 reads “not only within the Philippine Archipelago … but also outside of its jurisdiction”.
rpc.basis: Act No. 3815 as reproduced in the WIPO Lex / ChanRobles text; the “not only … but also” construction of the sentence

rpc.replace: but also by means of fault (culpa)
rpc.note: The source drops “by” (“but also means of fault”). Restored to “but also by means of fault (culpa)”.
rpc.basis: Act No. 3815 as reproduced in standard texts; parallel with “by means of deceit (dolo)”

civil.find: When the courts declared a law
civil.replace: When the courts declare a law
civil.note: The source reads “declared”; RA 386 reads “When the courts declare a law to be inconsistent with the Constitution”.
The text here correctly reads “situated”. Your uploaded Civil Code PDF reads “stipulated” at this point — that is a transcription error in that copy; the rule is lex situs.

civil.find: another in manner that is contrary
civil.replace: another in a manner that is contrary
civil.note: The source drops “a” (“in manner”). RA 386 reads “in a manner that is contrary to morals, good customs or public policy”.
Source note normalised to lower case, as printed elsewhere in the Code.

paras: Separation of property may refer to present or future property or both. It may be total or partial. In the latter case, the property not agreed upon as separate shall pertain to the conjugal partnership of gains.
civil.note: Restored: Article 213 is missing from the source transcription. The Code Commission source note is not shown because it could not be verified.
civil.basis: RA 386, Art. 213, as reproduced in standard codal compilations (first sentence verified against two independent copies)

paras: The obligation to give support shall be demandable from the time the person who has a right to receive the same needs it for maintenance, but it shall not be paid except from the date it is extrajudicially demanded.
civil.note: Restored: the source merged Article 298 into Article 297 and dropped its first paragraph. The second paragraph (“Payment shall be made monthly…”) has been moved back to Article 298.
civil.basis: RA 386, Art. 298, as quoted in Baltazar v. Serfino, G.R. No. L-17315 (1965)

paras: The owner of a parcel of land is the owner of its surface and of everything under it, and he can construct thereon any works or make any plantations and excavations which he may deem proper, without detriment to servitudes and subject to special laws and ordinances. He cannot complain of the reasonable requirements of aerial navigation. (350a)
civil.note: Restored: Article 437 is missing from the source transcription.
civil.basis: RA 386, Art. 437, as quoted in NPC v. Ibrahim (2007) and standard codal compilations

paras: Expenses for pure luxury or mere pleasure shall not be refunded to the possessor in good faith; but he may remove the ornaments with which he has embellished the principal thing if it suffers no injury thereby, and if his successor in the possession does not prefer to refund the amount expended. (454)
civil.note: Restored: Article 548 is missing from the source transcription. Check this one against your printed codal.
civil.basis: RA 386, Art. 548, as reproduced in standard codal compilations

paras: The usufructuary of an action to recover real property or a real right, or any movable property, has the right to bring the action and to oblige the owner thereof to give him the authority for this purpose and to furnish him whatever proof he may have. If in consequence of the enforcement of the action he acquires the thing claimed, the usufruct shall be limited to the fruits, the dominion remaining with the owner. (486)
civil.note: Restored: Article 578 is missing from the source transcription.
civil.basis: RA 386, Art. 578, as reproduced in standard codal compilations (opening and closing words verified against independent copies)

paras: The contract shall be presumed to be an equitable mortgage, in any of the following cases:
civil.move_from_prefix: (1) When the price of a sale
civil.note: Restored: the source dropped the opening sentence of Article 1602 and attached its six cases and final paragraph to Article 1601. They have been moved back.
civil.basis: RA 386, Art. 1602, as quoted in Supreme Court decisions (e.g., G.R. No. L-20901, Aug. 31, 1965)

paras: Whenever a piece of urban land which is so small and so situated that a major portion thereof cannot be used for any practical purpose within a reasonable time, having been bought merely for speculation, is about to be re-sold, the owner of any adjoining land has a right of pre-emption at a reasonable price.
civil.move_from_prefix: If the re-sale has been perfected
civil.note: Restored: the source dropped the first paragraph of Article 1622 and attached its last two paragraphs to Article 1621. They have been moved back.
civil.basis: RA 386, Art. 1622, as quoted in Ortega v. Orcine, G.R. No. L-28317 (1971)

paras: When a credit or other incorporeal right in litigation is sold, the debtor shall have a right to extinguish it by reimbursing the assignee for the price the latter paid therefor, the judicial costs incurred by him, and the interest on the price from the day on which the same was paid.
civil.move_from_prefix: A credit or other incorporeal right
civil.note: Restored: the source dropped the first paragraph of Article 1634 and attached the rest to Article 1633. Check the first paragraph against your printed codal.
civil.basis: RA 386, Art. 1634, as reproduced in standard codal compilations

paras: A sub-guarantor, in case of the insolvency of the guarantor for whom he bound himself, is responsible to the co-guarantors in the same terms as the guarantor. (1846)
civil.note: Restored: Article 2075 is missing from the source transcription.
civil.basis: RA 386, Art. 2075, as reproduced in standard codal compilations (opening words verified)

paras: If a third party secures an obligation by pledging his own movable property under the provisions of article 2085 he shall have the same rights as a guarantor under articles 2066 to 2070, and articles 2077 to 2081. He is not prejudiced by any waiver of defense by the principal obligor. (n)
civil.note: Restored: Article 2120 is missing from the source transcription.
civil.basis: RA 386, Art. 2120, as reproduced in two independent codal compilations
